faq: Can you open the account for me?
You open it, because Amazon verifies your identity, tax and bank details and these must be yours. We guide each screen, and then you add us as a user with the permissions the work needs.
What about gated categories and brands?
Some categories and brands need approval from Amazon. We explain what is required and prepare your documents list, but approval is Amazon's decision and we cannot promise it.
Can you get my account verified faster?
No one can. Verification takes the time Amazon needs. We make sure your documents are clear, complete and matching, so the first attempt is less likely to be rejected.
Do I need a registered business?
Not always. Amazon has individual and professional plans, and the right one depends on how much you plan to sell. We explain the difference, and the fees on each, before you choose.
desc:
Amazon Seller Central account setup help from Ecom Swift LLC walks you through opening your account and configuring it for selling. You enter your own identity, tax and bank details, and we guide each step and set up the settings around them.

## What does Amazon Seller Central setup involve?

Seller Central is the dashboard where you list products, manage orders and see payments. Setup means choosing a seller plan, registering in your own name or company, passing identity and payment verification, and then configuring the marketplaces, shipping, returns and fulfilment options. Only then can you create a listing that buyers can order.

Amazon verifies the identity, tax and bank details itself, so these must come from you. We do not enter them for you. We explain what each screen asks, what documents to have ready and what the common mistakes are.

## Why a careful setup saves trouble later

A rushed setup creates problems that are slow to fix. A name that does not match your documents can stall verification. A wrong seller plan can cost more than it needs to. Shipping and return settings left at their defaults can lead to late shipments, refused returns and account health warnings in the first weeks.

Choices such as selling from your own stock or using Amazon's fulfilment service also shape your costs, your workload and the categories you can enter. Making them with the numbers in front of you avoids paying for a model that does not suit your product.

## How setup affects your first months

A clean account reaches its first sale sooner and with fewer interruptions. When settings are correct from day one, your orders ship on time, your buyers see clear delivery and return terms, and your payments land in the right bank account. Those basics feed directly into the performance measures Amazon watches in a new account.

A launch plan matters as much as the settings. Knowing which product to list first, how to price it and what to watch in the first month gives a new seller direction. Results still depend on your product, price and competition, and we make no promises about sales.

## What a well-prepared account includes

- The right seller plan and account type for your business.
- Verification completed with documents that match exactly.
- Marketplaces chosen to fit where you can ship and be paid.
- Shipping templates that match your real handling and carrier times.
- Return settings that follow Amazon's rules for your category.
- A clear choice between self-shipping and Amazon's fulfilment service.
- Category approval requirements explained before you buy stock.
- A first listing prepared as a draft.
- A written launch plan and first-month checklist.

## How we guide you

We start with a short conversation about what you plan to sell, where you live and how you will ship. From that we recommend a seller plan and an order of steps. During verification we stay on hand to explain each field while you type your own details.

Once the account is open, we configure the settings that sit around it, set up shipping and return templates, and explain the fees you will meet. Higher packages add category and fulfilment decisions, listing drafts, an explanation of Brand Registry steps and a handover call. We work through the screens with you, and you stay in control of the account.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Use your real legal name and business details exactly as written on your documents.
- Have identity papers, a bank statement and a credit card ready before you start.
- Decide your fulfilment method before you order stock.
- Read the category requirements before you buy products.
- Keep a record of every verification email.

**Avoid:**
- Sharing your account login with anyone.
- Opening more than one account for the same business.
- Using details that belong to another person.
- Buying stock for a gated category before you are approved.
- Leaving shipping and return settings on their defaults.

## Who this is for

This service suits a first-time seller who is unsure where to begin and wants a clear path. It also suits a business owner who already sells online and now wants to add Amazon without costly mistakes. A small company moving from another marketplace can use it to set the right fulfilment model from the start.

## What we need from you

Send a short description of your products, your business type and your target marketplace. You do the verification steps yourself, and we guide you on a call or in messages. We never need your password, and any access we use later is given by you as a user invitation with limited permissions.
